reading: Ice versus water is the biggest switch. For 102 of 149 genomes the main axis of within-genome variation separates ice from water, more than winter (29) or pool (18). After dosing, ice and water states differ significantly in 78 of 85 testable genomes in 2024-25 and 96 of 104 in 2025-26. The same population behaves differently in brine than in the water below.

Sulfurimonas differs between pools, but not because of diesel. semibin_088 has one of the strongest pool separations (R² 0.42), yet the diesel-pool water moved less from its own pre-dosing state than the control did (shift 0.5×). The pools carry different strains of this genome (see Sulfur & hydrogen), which this method cannot tell apart from physiology. Along PC1 it trades ribosomal proteins (r +0.90) against motility and chemotaxis (r -0.92), and it slides from the growth end to the motile end through the 2025-26 season in both pools (growth index 98→38‰ diesel, 115→31‰ control).

Cycloclasticus lorbin_184 slows as its bloom ages. Its growth index falls over the 2025-26 diesel season (67→44‰). Its main axis sets hydrocarbon-degradation genes (r +0.45) and storage (r +0.59) against chaperones and proteases (r -0.37). Diesel-pool samples move along it with time (r -0.68 with day).

The 2024-25 Cycloclasticus (metabat_9342) moves between growth and scavenging. Its PC1 sets ribosomal proteins (r -0.78) and cold-shock proteins (r -0.85) against motility (r +0.65), transporters (r +0.77), storage (r +0.74) and nitrogen acquisition (r +0.89): a fast-growth state versus a foraging, nutrient-limited state.

50-400-T64 is still in growth mode at the end. Its growth index rises slightly over the 2025-26 diesel season (65→81‰), consistent with its late bloom (see the 50-400-T64 page). Its main axis pairs chaperones (r +0.71), oxidative-stress (r +0.77) and cold-shock genes against transporters (r -0.85) and nitrogen acquisition (r -0.85).

Background heterotrophs slow down in the diesel pool. Two abundant genomes that do not eat diesel lose growth-index share in the diesel pool but not in the control in 2025-26: Sulfitobacter metabat_5376 (142→96‰ diesel, 161→155‰ control; shift 1.9×, R² 0.05, q = 0.095) and UBA9145 vamb_4149 (80→53‰ diesel, 74→81‰ control). In UBA9145, phage-shock (psp) genes load strongly on PC1 (r -0.78), the same envelope-stress response seen on the Metals & toxicity page.

What this cannot do. Genomes that are abundant in only one pool (the blooming Cycloclasticus and 50-400-T64) cannot be compared between pools, because the control has too few reads on them. A MAG can hide several strains, and different strains in different pools or winters look like different states. Nitrosopumilus had too few reads for a profile. One pool per treatment, so no test separates diesel from other pool differences.
